<!-- head-1: body_md -->
When every problem uses a different shape ($K{=}1$), NHMO pays its geometry step (Table~\ref{tab:runtime}) for every problem; on a new mesh-based shape this step is cheaper than meshing, whereas on grid inputs the grid-based baselines need no such step. (ii) Training is a separate concern (Appendix~\ref{app:train-cost}). The speed advantage is at deployment, where the system is queried many times against the same geometries.
<!-- end head-1 -->
